subject: Reserved capacity: burst-credit construct + tenor-flex proposal for Velox
messages:
From: Alyssa King <alyssa@velox.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@velox.ai
Date: 2028-04-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing + pricing ask for reserved capacity (Velox)

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our CTO and infra team ran a quick spike and we have a clearer sense of steady-state vs burst needs. Before we move into legal/procurement, procurement asked for a proposal that does three things:

- Keeps a 12–18 month committed pool but allows for a defined burst window (30% above baseline) for Q4 launch traffic spikes.
- Protects us from sharp GPU spot price moves with a pricing corridor or credit so we don't exceed forecasted TCO.
- Keeps activation scheduling flexible (phased activation across regions).

I've attached our preliminary usage profile and asked our finance lead Tom to join the thread for any procurement details. Can you send a short proposal that sketches the commit tenor, burst-credit construct, and any suggested safeguards (price collars/credits)? Also please highlight where you'd need exec approvals for discounts.

Thanks —
Alyssa
Director, Cloud Ops
Velox.ai

Attachments: Velox_usage_profile.csv (referenced), procurement-RFP.pdf (referenced)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa@velox.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing + pricing ask for reserved capacity (Velox)

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage files. High-level answer up front, details below and attached:

1) Tenor: We recommend a 12-month committed baseline for predictability, with an optional 6-12 month phased activation schedule across regions (you can ramp region-by-region to match your rollout).

2) Burst-credit construct: We can offer a pool of on-demand burst credits that allow up to +30% sustained capacity for short bursts (max 72 hours per month) charged at a blended burst rate. Excess beyond credits billed at a predefined uplift.

3) Pricing safeguard: We can include a GPU-cost corridor: if average GPU exchange pricing (index we track) moves >15% above baseline, we either trigger a credit fund (one-time debit to your account) or a price collar that reduces uplift for the next billing period. Exec approval required for credit size >$150k or for changing the trigger threshold.

4) Discounts and approvals: We can propose a tiered discount tied to committed vCPU/GPU hours and a one-time onboarding credit. Anything that pushes effective price below our standard reserved SKU floor requires VP Pricing sign-off (I can route).

I've attached: the sensitivity model (GPU_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx) with three scenarios, and an annotated SOW draft (Velox_SOW_v3.pdf). Karthik/Monica/Kimberly — please review the proposed approval path below and flag any legal/finance must-haves we should bake in before sending to Velox.

Quick ask for Velox: can you confirm target regions (us-west-2, us-east-1 or both) and the expected Q4 peak date range? That will change the recommended buffer sizing and activation timing.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: GPU_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx, Velox_SOW_v3.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alyssa King <alyssa@velox.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing + pricing ask for reserved capacity (Velox)

Looping in some commercial detail — Alyssa, thanks for the clarity. Short clarifications from our side:

- Baseline sizing: we recommend locking 500 reserved GPU-hours/day as a baseline (region split configurable). Burst credits of 150 GPU-hours/day available for up to 72h/month.
- Billing: baseline billed as monthly committed; burst credits consumed first, then on-demand with a 30% uplift relative to baseline rate.
- Credit fund vs collar: credit fund (capped) is simpler operationally — we can set a $100k fund that applies when the index > +15%. A collar implies dynamic pricing adjustments and requires legal to allow index-based billing language.

Kimberly / Monica — for internal routing: if Velox wants the $100k credit fund plus a 10% up-front onboarding discount, that will require Finance and VP Pricing sign-off. Anything above $100k credit will need CRO/COO approval. Monica, any redline items we should anticipate on the collar language?

Thanks — I can package a short two-page commercial summary if that helps.

—Karthik

From: Alyssa King <alyssa@velox.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rafferty <tom.rafferty@velox.ai>, procurement@velox.ai
Date: 2028-04-23T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing + pricing ask for reserved capacity (Velox)

Marcus / Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the model. We reviewed the sensitivity workbook and prefer the credit fund approach for simplicity. A few follow-ups from procurement:

- Velox prefers a 12-month baseline with phased region activation (start us-west-2, add us-east-1 in month 4).
- The $100k credit fund is acceptable to start, with a review clause at month 6 tied to actual usage vs forecast.
- We will push for a modest ~8% onboarding credit; understand anything shy of 10% needs additional approvals.
- Please include a clause that caps billed burst uplift to no more than 45% over baseline for any single invoice (procurement wants a hard cap).

Next steps: send an updated SOW and a proposed redline (we'll have legal push back on any index-based automatic billing adjustments — so keep language conservative). If you can get the SOW + redline to us by Friday I can fast-track procurement review.

Tom / procurement — I'll attach the SOW to our internal tender. Marcus / team — curious on rough timing for internal pricing approvals if we request the 8% onboarding credit and the $100k credit fund (i.e., who signs off and how long).

Thanks —
Alyssa
